planting.note: Set container-grown plants out in spring once soil is workable; no trellis is needed since this is a non-climbing, self-supporting form.

directions: Expander was bred by Szczepan Marczynski at his Polish nursery Zrodlo Dobrych Pnaczy and released in 2025, carrying medium-sized dark pink blooms on the compact Integrifolia Group it belongs to. Like other solitary clematis it forms a lax, non-vining clump rather than climbing, so let it sprawl at the front of a border or weave through sturdier perennial neighbors for support. Cut the whole plant down to a few inches above the soil in late winter, since every season's flowers come entirely from new growth.

planting.note: Plant in spring in well-drained soil; no climbing support is required for this mounding, herbaceous clematis.

directions: Introduced in 2025 by Polish breeder Szczepan Marczynski at Zrodlo Dobrych Pnaczy, Sweet Wave carries violet-blue, nodding bell flowers held over a tidy clump of simple leaves. As with all Integrifolia Group clematis it does not climb, so plant it where it can lean on neighboring perennials or spill over a low edge. Shear the dead stems to the ground in late winter to clear the way for fresh flowering growth.

planting.note: Set out in spring in average, well-drained garden soil; this herbaceous selection needs no trellis.

directions: Friendship is one of the newest Integrifolia Group selections from Szczepan Marczynski's Polish clematis breeding program, introduced for 2026 with clear violet blooms held on a low, non-climbing clump. Grow it toward the front of a mixed border or let it scramble through the stems of a nearby shrub for informal support, since the species never develops true clinging tendrils. Cut all growth back to ground level in late winter to reset the plant for its next summer flush.

planting.note: Plant container stock in spring; no support structure is needed for this mounding, non-vining clematis.

directions: Released for 2026 by Szczepan Marczynski's Zrodlo Dobrych Pnaczy nursery in Poland, Pink Horizon is prized for smothering its clump in single pink flowers more profusely than many older Integrifolia Group selections. It stays a lax, self-supporting mound rather than climbing, so site it where it can tumble over a low wall or weave through sturdier perennials. Cut the entire plant to a few inches above the ground in late winter, since it blooms only on the current year's new stems.

planting.note: Plant in spring in well-drained soil; this non-climbing form needs no trellis, only nearby plants to lean on.

directions: Bred by Szczepan Marczynski and introduced in 2024, Once More opens unusually large flowers for the Integrifolia Group, roughly 4-5 inches across, in deep violet with a purple central stripe on each of its 5-6 twirled tepals. It forms the characteristic lax, non-vining clump of this group rather than true climbing growth, so give it neighboring shrubs or perennials to drape over. Cut all stems to the ground in late winter, since the following season's bloom comes entirely from fresh growth.

planting.note: Set out in spring; no climbing support is required, only nearby plants or a low edge for the stems to lean against.

directions: Strawberry Fields, introduced in 2024 by Polish breeder Szczepan Marczynski, carries single, medium-sized dark red-pink flowers. As with its Integrifolia Group relatives it never develops clinging tendrils, instead forming a self-supporting clump best used scrambling through the front of a border or over a low wall. Shear the dead growth to the ground each late winter to make way for the next summer's display.
